issues.legal_issue: Land classified as Brahmottar and held by qualifying landholders under the applicable land tenure regime is heritable and transferable without a restriction limiting transfers to a specified class.
material_facts: The lands were described as Brahmottar in the revenue records.
The transferors had held the lands under the Government for the required continuous period and had paid revenue or held under an express exemption from revenue.
The claimant alleged that the lands had been granted for temple service and could be transferred only to temple officials.
The challenged transfers were to persons outside the class the claimant said was permitted to receive the lands.
issues.conclusion: The lands were heritable and transferable without restriction, so the alleged class-based limit did not invalidate the transfers.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(g), 8(1)(a), and 9 of the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886, qualifying holders became landholders with permanent, heritable, and transferable rights of use and occupancy. This statutory result was consistent with the Government of India’s recognition in 1879 that the relevant holdings were heritable and transferable. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.transfer_challenge_suit: A claimant brought a suit challenging land transfers as invalid because of an alleged restriction on transferability.
predicates.brahmottar_revenue_classification: The land was described as Brahmottar in revenue records.
predicates.qualifying_longstanding_landholding: The holder had held the land under the Government continuously for the required period and had paid revenue or held under an express revenue exemption.
predicates.land_transfers_are_unrestricted: The land is heritable and transferable without the alleged restriction.

issues.definition: When a transfer-challenge suit concerns land recorded as Brahmottar and held under the qualifying longstanding conditions, the land transfers are unrestricted.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant alleging that land could be transferred only to a specified class bears the burden of proving that restriction.
material_facts: The claimant asserted that the lands could be transferred only to temple officials and challenged transfers to others.
The High Court held that the claimant, rather than the transferees, had to prove the alleged restriction.
The Supreme Court upheld that allocation of the burden.
issues.conclusion: The claimant bore the burden of proving the alleged restriction.
issues.legal_principle: The party asserting a limitation on the otherwise recognized transferability of land must prove that limitation. The Court relied on the statutory recognition of the holders’ transferable rights under sections 3(g), 8(1)(a), and 9 of the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886, and cited no earlier cases on the burden of proof.

predicates.transfer_restriction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim that land transfers were invalid because transferability was limited.
predicates.claimant_asserts_class_limited_transfera: The claimant alleged that the land could be transferred only to a specified class of persons.
predicates.claimant_bears_burden_of_proof: The claimant must prove the alleged limitation on transferability.

issues.definition: In a proceeding where a claimant asserts that land could be transferred only to a specified class, the claimant bears the burden of proving that limitation.

issues.legal_issue: Insufficient evidence, consisting largely of hearsay and inadequate even if accepted, does not establish an alleged restriction on land transfers.
material_facts: The claimant relied on evidence that the courts below had treated as proving a service obligation and a restriction on transfers.
The evidence was largely hearsay and meagre, and the Supreme Court considered it legally insufficient even if believed.
The claimant bore the burden of proving the alleged restriction.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not establish any restriction on transferability.
issues.legal_principle: The party alleging a restriction on transferability bears the burden of proving it, and evidence that is legally insufficient cannot satisfy that burden. The Court applied sections 3(g), 8(1)(a), and 9 of the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886, which recognized the relevant holders’ transferable rights; it relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.transfer_restriction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim that land transfers were invalid because transferability was limited.
predicates.claimant_asserts_class_limited_transfera: The claimant alleged that the land could be transferred only to a specified class of persons.
predicates.evidence_is_hearsay_and_legally_insuffic: The claimant's evidence was largely hearsay and was legally insufficient even if accepted.
predicates.restriction_not_established: The alleged restriction on transferability is not proved.

issues.definition: When a claimant asserting a class-based restriction in a transfer challenge relies on evidence that is largely hearsay and legally insufficient, the restriction is not established.
